interface.title: FLIM Playground – Data Analysis
interface.field: Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) / single-cell metabolic imaging
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis of single-cell feature tables that have already been extracted from images: exploring them, testing them statistically, building figures and exporting reproducible scripts
interface.what_it_is_for: Upload a table of single-cell features, check how each column is read, then compare features across cell lines and treatments with strip and box plots, histograms with mixture-model fits, 2D scatters, dimension reduction and classifiers, and export the analysis as a standalone Python script.

data.note: inhibitors_demo.csv: 24 cells × 31 columns (cell_id; categorical image_name, cell_line [MCF7, PANC-1], treatment [Control, Inhibitor_A, Inhibitor_B], dish; NADH and FAD lifetime t1/t2/a1/tm/tm_iw, morphology, intensity, redox_ratio_nadh_fad, fit diagnostics). Lifetime fit_nadh: t1 has a NaN, and the app warns about it. The file has no free-fit phasor columns ('Lifetime fit free_<channel>: G(1st)/S(1st)'), so the app's phasor view was not offered.

tree.general: Find out how cell metabolism features differ between groups of cells and keep a reproducible record of the analysis
tree.specific: Compare NADH/FAD lifetime and redox features across MCF7 vs PANC-1 cells under Control, Inhibitor_A and Inhibitor_B, and export the analysis as a Python script

features.name: Column role and group editor
features.general: After loading a table, check each column's guessed type, change the types of several columns at once, and sort numeric columns into named groups before any analysis
features.specific: Bulk Column Role Assignment plus Feature Group Management: tick rows, give them Categorical/Numerical/Ignore, create groups with ➕ New group and fill them with 'Move N', rename or delete groups from the ✏️ popover, then press 'Use for this upload' or 'Save profile as'
steps: Read the guessed Role, Group and value preview for each column
Tick one or more rows (or Select all)
Choose a role in 'Ticked columns are' and press the apply button (e.g. 'Ignore 1')
Make a group with ➕ New group and move ticked Numerical rows into it with 'Move N'
Rename or delete a group from the ✏️ popover
Confirm with 'Use for this upload' or save the settings as a named profile
serves_tasks: Check the guessed type of each column
Sort related measurements into a named group
Leave an irrelevant column out of the analysis
Confirm the column settings and start the analysis

features.name: Grouped feature picker
features.general: Choose a measurement from short dropdowns, one per family of related measurements, instead of from one long list
features.specific: Sidebar dropdowns, one per feature group (Lifetime fit_nadh, Lifetime fit_fad, Redox, …). Picking a value sets the plotted feature; Bivariate mode asks for an x-axis and then a y-axis
steps: Open the dropdown for a feature group
Pick a feature (e.g. nadh: tm)
In Bivariate mode, pick an x-axis feature, then a y-axis feature from the next set of pickers
In Multivariate mode, pick several features per group (All by default)
serves_tasks: Plot one measurement for each group
Plot two measurements against each other, by group
Reduce many measurements to two axes and see whether groups separate

features.name: Group comparison plot with significance brackets
features.general: Plot one measurement for every group, split by a second factor, add box summaries, and mark pairwise effect sizes and test results
features.specific: Feature Comparison: strip plot with Color by, Separate by, Collapse by, Boxplot overlay (resets to None and is dropped when Separate by changes), Connect means, an effect-size choice (Glass's Delta or Cohen's d), a t-test choice (Independent or Welch's) and comparison pairs
steps: Pick a feature and a Color by category
Optionally Separate by a second category into panels
Add a Boxplot overlay and/or Connect means
Choose an effect-size method and a t-test, then the comparison pairs
Optionally Collapse by image to compare per-image means (stats are skipped when a group has fewer than two points)
serves_tasks: Plot one measurement for each group
Show summary statistics over the points
Split the comparison by a second factor
Test whether the differences between groups are significant
Average the cells within each image before comparing

features.name: Histogram with mixture-model subpopulations
features.general: Draw the distribution of a measurement per group, fit a Gaussian mixture to find subpopulations, adjust the fit, and export each item's subpopulation label
features.specific: Feature Histogram: bin width and Log X, skew per group; Apply Gaussian Mixture Model with Max Components and Min Weight Threshold sliders; subgroup table (rename by double-click) with H-index; 'Download GMM Grouped Data' adds a GMM_group column
steps: Pick a feature and a Color by category; adjust Bin Width
Tick Apply Gaussian Mixture Model
Set Max Components and Min Weight Threshold
Read the means, SDs and weights of each subgroup and the H-index; optionally rename subgroups
Name the export column and download the labelled CSV
serves_tasks: Look at the shape of a measurement's distribution
Find subpopulations within each group
Save each item's subpopulation label

features.name: 2D scatter with regression, marginals and 2D GMM
features.general: Plot two measurements against each other by group, report correlation, fit a regression line, add marginal distributions, and fit 2D mixture components
features.specific: 2D Feature Distribution: Pearson r for each group, Regression line (R², slope, intercept), Marginal Plot Type (gaussian fit, boxplot or violin), 2D Gaussian Mixture Model with component sliders and a subgroup table, Log X/Log Y
steps: Pick the x and y features
Read Pearson r and p for each group
Tick Regression line
Choose a marginal plot type
Tick 2D Gaussian Mixture Model and set the components
serves_tasks: Plot two measurements against each other, by group
Fit a trend and show each axis's distribution

features.name: Dimension reduction embedding
features.general: Project many measurements onto two axes with a choice of method, and encode groups by colour, shape and opacity to see whether they separate
features.specific: Dimension Reduction: UMAP (n_neighbors, min_dist), PCA (explained variance shown on the axes) or t-SNE, with Color by, Shape by, Opacity by and Separate by
steps: Choose the feature groups (or subsets) to include
Choose UMAP, PCA or t-SNE and set its parameters
Set Color by and Shape by to two categories
Look for separation in the embedding
serves_tasks: Reduce many measurements to two axes and see whether groups separate

features.name: Classifier evaluation panel
features.general: Train a classifier to tell two groups apart from the measurements and judge it with metrics, an ROC curve, a confusion matrix and feature importances
features.specific: Classification: Classify by category, choice of pair, Random Forest / Gradient Boosting / SVM / Logistic Regression, train size, sampling method, class weight, threshold tuning; shows overall and per-class metrics, ROC, confusion matrix and feature importances. Logistic Regression stops with 'Input X contains NaN' when a selected feature has missing values
steps: Choose the Classify by category and which pair to classify
Choose a classifier and its hyperparameters, and the train size
Optionally set the sampling, class weight and threshold tuning
Read the metrics, ROC curve, confusion matrix and feature importances
serves_tasks: Test how well the measurements predict group membership

features.name: Plot styling
features.general: Adjust a figure's point size, fonts, colours and legend counts
features.specific: Plot Styling panel below each plot: point size, axis and legend font sizes, Color Map, show group counts (n) in the legend
steps: Set point size and font sizes
Choose a colour map
Optionally show group counts (n) in the legend

features.name: Export a reproducible script
features.general: Export the whole analysis, with its current settings, as a standalone script
features.specific: 'Export the entire analysis as a Python script' button under Plot Styling in every module
steps: Set up the analysis in any module
Press 'Export the entire analysis as a Python script'
serves_tasks: Export code that reproduces the current analysis
